# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

**Investigated**: The existing formatISO implementation and its test file (src/format-iso.test.ts) were read to establish the output contract. The parse() function was inspected for its length guard, its regex, and its NaN-versus-throw behavior. The working branch was confirmed as feat/iso-duration.

**Learned**: formatISO rounds input to whole milliseconds, prefixes negatives with "-", omits zero components, and strips trailing zeros from fractional seconds. parse() throws on a length over 100 but its message says "between 1 and 99", an off-by-one mismatch. parse() returns NaN for regex mismatches, not an exception.

**Completed**: parseISO is added and exported from src/index.ts. It accepts weeks, days, hours, minutes, and seconds, an optional leading "-", decimals with "." or ",", and lowercase input. It returns NaN for years, months, and malformed strings, including "P", "PT", "P1DT", "PT30M1H", "P1H", and "PT1D". It throws for non-string, empty, or over-100-character input. A trailing-T guard that an earlier sed command had failed to remove was simplified with an edit. The new test file src/parse-iso.test.ts covers the valid forms, the NaN cases, the throw paths, and a round-trip over ten values that includes negative and sub-second inputs. The full jest run passes at 188 tests with 100% coverage, and tsc and biome check are clean. biome format rewrote src/index.ts during the run. Nothing is committed yet, and pnpm test:edge was not run.

**Next Steps**: Decide whether to commit parseISO and its tests on feat/iso-duration. Decide whether to add a README section covering formatISO and parseISO.

**Notes**: The parseISO error message repeats the "between 1 and 99" wording although the guard permits 100 characters, carried over from parse(). The open question about the trailing-zero regex in formatISO is still unresolved and was not changed in this session. The current working tree has src/index.ts modified and src/parse-iso.test.ts untracked.
